review_type: Independent local provider-neutral identity, namespace compatibility and public artifact review

checks: Fresh generic installation creates no legacy persistent namespace and uses the generic wrapper
An exact recognized legacy prelaunch payload refreshes within the same legacy namespace, archives old code and creates no generic base
Mixed or dangling opposite namespaces refuse before payload writes; namespace changes during staging prevent commit
Machine-id validation, absent firmware UUID, firmware placeholders and recorded machine/firmware drift behave explicitly
Schema1 jobs are refused before identity adoption; existing job schema is never silently upgraded
A dangling job checkpoint is preserved by direct apply admission
An opposite systemd unit still loaded without unit files blocks both installer and core

combined_validation_observed.scope: Parent-run combined regression result read from the hash-bound validation manifest; independent checks listed separately

actual_Python36_evidence.interpreter: Canonical-authenticated CPython3.6.9 privately extracted without package installation
checks: Eleven bootstrap/helper modules compile and import, including generic layout and local identity
Mocked Bionic-to-Focal planning, pre-Noble PHP rejection and package logging remain compatible
Local identity capture and drift rejection run without metadata access
The exact inline bootstrap and helper definitions execute after excluding the final production install/apply call; start=False installation uses only temporary fixture paths
The delivered offline release verifier passes

findings_fixed: Direct launch could overwrite a dangling job-state symlink
An opposite-name systemd unit retained in the manager after file deletion was not previously checked
preserved_controls: Exact supported adjacent Ubuntu release paths and postboot acceptance
Authenticated package plans, protected database compatibility lines and runtime/configuration health checks
No replacement of queued, running, failed or interrupted jobs
Recognized prelaunch code hashes, archives, admission locks and process checks
Legacy prelaunch deployment stays in its original namespace rather than migrating jobs
limits: Local fixtures and extracted Python do not reproduce every production bootloader, architecture, native APT or application environment
Machine-id alone is not clone-resistant when no valid firmware UUID is available
A recorded firmware UUID that disappears or changes holds; malformed or unreadable identity evidence is not silently ignored
Provider neutrality removes mandatory metadata/account prerequisites but does not waive existing compatibility, database, recovery or failed-job holds
Existing legacy job states remain bound to their original updater and are not upgraded to the new schema
Optional known provider repositories remain source-compatibility profiles, not prerequisites
No universal Ubuntu compatibility, live release success, tested recovery or complete vulnerability-closure claim is made
Runtime logs, collected host identifiers and configuration backups remain private
